title: Finding the Patients Who Respond
subtitle: How CrisPRO identified a patient subgroup where STC-1010 outperforms every standard option

data_sources.primary: CRC mechanism-fit ranker (TCGA COADREAD MSS cohort, n=485)
data_sources.ceacam5_corpus: 5-trial failure corpus with IHC threshold analysis

stages.name: The Problem
stages.plain_language: Colorectal cancer that is microsatellite stable (MSS) rarely responds to immunotherapy. About 95% of metastatic colorectal cancer patients have MSS tumors. Standard chemotherapy helps, but no targeted immunotherapy has worked for this group. The question for any new drug is: which patients might actually benefit?

stages.name: How CrisPRO Analyzes a Drug
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO reads the scientific literature and clinical trial results for a drug, then builds a profile of how that drug works — what biological pathways it targets, what resistance mechanisms it overcomes, and what patient characteristics make it more or less likely to work. For STC-1010, CrisPRO identified that its core mechanism is immune activation: it trains the immune system to attack the tumor by presenting tumor proteins and triggering an immune response.

data_shown.mechanism_summary: Whole-cell therapeutic vaccine that presents over 200 tumor proteins to the immune system, combined with low-dose cyclophosphamide (removes immune brakes) and GM-CSF (activates immune scouts). The vaccine also uses a chemical tag (hapten) that draws immune cells into the tumor.

stages.name: Scoring 485 Real Patients Against 8 Treatment Options
stages.plain_language: CrisPRO scored 485 real MSS colorectal cancer patients from the TCGA database against STC-1010 and 7 standard treatment regimens used in colorectal cancer. Each patient gets a fit score from 0 to 1 for each treatment — higher means the treatment is a better match for that patient's tumor biology. The 7 comparators are major clinical trial regimens: MOSAIC, N0147, PRIME, PEAK, PACCE, HORIZON III, and VELOUR.

data_shown.overall_result: STC-1010 ranks 3rd or 4th for 98.1% of patients. PRIME and PEAK dominate because they target a pathway (MAPK) that is active in nearly all MSS tumors.

stages.name: The Breakthrough: Finding the Responders
stages.plain_language: When CrisPRO filtered for patients with high tumor mutational burden (TMB >= 25 mutations per megabase), STC-1010 jumped to first place for every single patient in that subgroup. All 9 patients with TMB >= 25 ranked STC-1010 as their best option — ahead of every standard treatment. This is the responder signal: a specific, identifiable patient population where the investigational drug outperforms all comparators.

subgroups.name: All MSS patients
subgroups.interpretation: STC-1010 loses to PRIME/PEAK in the broad population

subgroups.name: TMB >= 25 mut/Mb
subgroups.interpretation: STC-1010 is the top-ranked treatment for every patient in this subgroup

data_shown.key_metric: recall_at_3 = 1.0 means STC-1010 appears in the top 3 recommendations for 100% of high-TMB patients
data_shown.clinical_anchor: This aligns with CCTG CO.26, where patients with plasma TMB >= 28 showed the strongest immunotherapy survival benefit (OS HR 0.34) — the best published immunotherapy signal in MSS CRC.

stages.name: Why It Works: The Biology
stages.plain_language: STC-1010's core mechanism is immune activation. In most MSS patients, the immune system is 'asleep' — tumors have low mutation burden, so there are few targets for the immune system to recognize. But in high-TMB patients, the tumor has many mutations, creating many potential immune targets. STC-1010's vaccine approach amplifies this existing vulnerability: it trains the immune system against the tumor's proteins, and the high mutation burden means there are more targets to attack. Standard treatments like PRIME target a different pathway (cell growth signaling) that doesn't benefit from high TMB.

data_shown.explanation: In high-TMB patients, the immune activation component of STC-1010's score becomes dominant. At TMB >= 25, the immune axis contributes the majority of the fit score, pushing STC-1010 above all comparators.
data_shown.crossover_point: STC-1010 overtakes PRIME when the immune axis score reaches 0.44, which corresponds to approximately TMB = 30 mut/Mb. In this dataset, the 9 high-TMB patients all have TMB between 102 and 382 mut/Mb.

pathway_comparison.PRIME: Cell growth signaling (MAPK — active in all MSS tumors regardless of TMB)
pathway_comparison.N0147: Cell growth signaling + drug resistance (efflux — higher in HRD-High tumors)

stages.name: What CrisPRO Also Decoded: Learning From Failed Trials
stages.plain_language: Beyond the responder analysis, CrisPRO has decoded 42 clinical trials across 7 drug programs — extracting why each trial succeeded or failed. For the CEACAM5 program alone, CrisPRO analyzed 5 failed trials and identified 5 distinct failure modes: wrong patient selection criteria, archived tissue limitations, payload resistance, regulatory safety signals, and target toxicity. This intelligence helps avoid repeating the same mistakes.

ceacam5_failure_modes.finding: CEACAM5 protein threshold set too low (>=50%). The >=80% subgroup showed directional benefit. The trial failed because most enrolled patients did not have high enough CEACAM5 expression.
CEACAM5 expression was measured on archived biopsy tissue, not fresh tumor at enrollment. Tumor expression changes over time, so archived measurements may not reflect current status.
The drug delivered SN-38, the same active ingredient as irinotecan — a drug most patients had already received and developed resistance to. Response rate was only 1.2%.
European clinical hold due to safety concerns shared with a discontinued drug using the same linker chemistry. The safety signal is specific to the chemistry class, not the target.

The drug activated immune cells as designed (CD8+ T-cell infiltration confirmed), but response rate was only 13.5%. CEACAM5 is also expressed on normal gut tissue, causing on-target gastrointestinal toxicity that limits the achievable dose.

data_shown.ceacam5_key_finding: CEACAM5 protein levels are prognostic (correlate with outcome) but NOT predictive (do not identify who responds to CEACAM5-targeted therapy). PROCEADE-CRC-01 confirmed this: Spearman correlation -0.14, P=0.4 — no statistical relationship between CEACAM5 expression and treatment response.

stages.name: What This Means for Drug Development
stages.plain_language: For a pharma team evaluating STC-1010, CrisPRO's analysis points to a clear strategy: enrich the clinical trial for high-TMB MSS patients. In the broad MSS population, STC-1010 does not outperform standard care. But in the TMB >= 25 subgroup, it is the top-ranked option for every patient. This is the kind of biomarker-driven enrichment that can turn a failed trial into a successful one. The BreAK CRC-001 trial currently does not prospectively collect TMB — this is the critical design gap.

recommendations.action: Collect TMB prospectively in BreAK CRC-001
recommendations.rationale: The responder signal is confined to TMB >= 25. Without prospective TMB collection, the trial cannot confirm this subgroup benefit.

recommendations.action: Consider TMB-enriched enrollment for Phase 2 expansion
recommendations.rationale: If 100% of TMB >= 25 patients rank STC-1010 first, enriching for this subgroup could dramatically increase the probability of seeing a clinical signal.

recommendations.action: Use the CEACAM5 failure corpus to avoid selection mistakes
recommendations.rationale: The CEACAM5 program failed partly because the patient selection biomarker (IHC threshold) was set too low. STC-1010's TMB threshold must be validated prospectively.

data_shown.clinical_anchor: CCTG CO.26 showed that patients with plasma TMB >= 28 had OS HR 0.34 with dual checkpoint blockade — the strongest published immunotherapy signal in MSS CRC. STC-1010's mechanism-fit advantage in the same biology is consistent with this external evidence.

roadmap_items.description: CrisPRO is developing the ability to retroactively predict which patients responded in past clinical trials, using the same mechanism-fit approach. This is currently in validation.
